audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff said HARD while breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both said 'Even matchup - difficulty 5.5/10'. The page contradicted itself on the headline label.
audit.why: Emerald+ 65% over 20 games with a 5.5/10 difficulty rating is not a hard matchup. EVEN is the label the rest of the file already uses.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offered 'the fifteen-second invitation' on Across the Veil.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s - the invitation is twenty-two seconds at rank 1, and that gap is the entire matchup plan.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, report[9].t and loading now use 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (1) The content layer referred to 'her root' in six places - Aurora has no root anywhere in her kit; The Weirding and Between Worlds slow, Twofold Hex curses. (2) Across the Veil was labelled '(E)' in the content layer; it is her W, which the full layer already had right. (3) Between Worlds was never described - it creates a zone that only SLOWS and lets Aurora teleport across it. It is not a wall, so you can Riftwalk straight through.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'The Weirding ... damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward'; 'Between Worlds ... creates an area that slows enemies within it and allows Aurora to teleport from one side of the area to the other'. Nothing in the kit roots.
audit.corrected: Removed every root reference, relabelled Across the Veil as (W), and wrote the Between Worlds zone into report[5].t and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentioned anti-heal.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration exorcises spirits from everything she damages and those spirits heal her, so extended poke trades feed her sustain. Grievous Wounds is a real item slot in this lane.
audit.corrected: report[8].t and loading now call for anti-heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer called Aurora 'him'/'his' in tldr, tradeGood, dosFull[1], dontsFull[1] and report[3].t.
audit.why: Aurora is female; the content layer already used 'her'.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] said Force Pulse 'only charges as abilities are cast nearby, so you can't punish her'.
audit.why: That reads backwards here - Aurora casts constantly, so Force Pulse charges quickly. The actual reason you cannot punish is Force Pulse's 400 range against her 900-range Q.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[2] around the range gap instead.

edits.before: Aurora owns these levels and you concede them — that is the deal. Her Q pokes you from outside your range and her W spirit damage chips you while Null Sphere's shield sits on cooldown and your mana pool is empty, so do not trade, just last-hit with Q at max range and eat the harassment. The one thing you must respect is her root: if she lands it, your blinkless level-1-to-3 self has no escape from the follow-up burst. Stay behind minions, never walk up for a CS inside her Across the Veil (E) range, and treat every HP bar above half as a win.
edits.after: Aurora owns these levels and you concede them - that is the deal. Twofold Hex pokes you from 900 units and The Weirding chips and slows while Null Sphere's shield sits on cooldown and your mana pool is empty, so do not trade, just last-hit with Q at max range and eat the harassment. She has no root - what you respect is the slow into her full combo, because your blinkless level-1-to-3 self cannot walk out of it. Stay behind minions, never step up for a CS inside Across the Veil (W) range, and treat every HP bar above half as a win.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still hers — keep weathering it, throw Nether Blade (W) autos at the wave to bank mana, and farm under tower if she shoves. Level 6 is the turning point even though she still edges the raw lane: Riftwalk finally lets you sidestep her root by blinking out of the cast, and once her Across the Veil (E) blink is on cooldown you can R onto her, Q to shield her return poke, and trade back. Bait that E — she will burn it to escape your first blink, and the second it is down she is a stationary AP mage you can run straight at.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still hers - keep weathering it, throw Nether Blade (W) autos at the wave to bank mana, and farm under tower if she shoves. Level 6 is the turning point even though she still edges the raw lane: Riftwalk finally lets you leave The Weirding slow by blinking out of the cast, and once her Across the Veil (W) hop is on cooldown you can R onto her, Q to shield her return poke, and trade back. Bait that hop - she will burn it to escape your first blink, and the second it is down she is a stationary AP mage you can run straight at.

edits.before: This is the whole reason you suffered the lane. By 2+ items with Riftwalk maxed, Void Stone's 15% magic reduction plus your Q shield eat the bulk of her AP combo, and her root no longer kills you — it just delays you. You blink-spam onto her squishy frame, ramp Riftwalk to execute her before the combo finishes, and she cannot rebuild the spacing she lived on early. Unlike a true hyperscaler, Aurora does not reclaim this window — once you are full-build, your anti-mage profile makes her exactly the target you want.
